source_text: Num igitur ideo aut Libri sacri auctores probabuntur errorum, aut crimina pereuntium, Scripturarum dignitas expiabit?
pass_a_gloss: Will therefore either the authors of the sacred Books be proved authors of the errors, or will the dignity of the Scriptures wash away the crimes of those perishing?
pass_b_english: Will the sacred books therefore be proved to be the authors of their errors? Or will Scripture's dignity acquit those who are perishing of their crimes?

choices.why: Julian's sacred writings; keep Scripture, not 'Bible' as a later book-name.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
